# Momentum, reversal, and crashes

Cross-sectional momentum is measured with 12-1 momentum, skipping the most recent month to avoid
short-term reversal.

Momentum crashes follow market rebounds. Momentum contradicts the reversal effect at the
one-month horizon but not at the twelve-month horizon.

Time-series momentum extends cross-sectional momentum to futures and currencies. Trend following
uses time-series momentum as its core signal.

We report the maximum drawdown and the Sharpe ratio of both strategies, estimated with
Fama-MacBeth regressions on CRSP data.
